title: Go: Basic Goroutines
description: Learn to launch and manage goroutines for concurrent execution in Go.

steps.title: Launch a basic goroutine
steps.description: Use the `go` keyword to launch a function as a goroutine. Write a program that prints "Hello from goroutine" from a goroutine and "Hello from main" from main.
hints: Use `go myFunction()` to launch a goroutine
Add a small `time.Sleep` so the goroutine has time to run before main exits
The `go` keyword immediately returns — the calling thread does not wait

verification.test: output.includes('Hello from goroutine') && output.includes('Hello from main')
verification.successMessage: Great! Your goroutine ran and printed its message.
verification.failureMessage: Make sure both messages appear in the output.

steps.title: Anonymous goroutine
steps.description: Launch an anonymous function as a goroutine. Use `go func()` with no arguments to print "Anonymous goroutine running".
hints: Anonymous goroutines can close over variables from the enclosing scope
Remember to give the goroutine time to execute

verification.successMessage: Anonymous goroutines are a clean way to run quick concurrent tasks!
verification.failureMessage: Ensure you used an anonymous function with the go keyword.

steps.title: Multiple goroutines
steps.description: Launch 3 separate goroutines that each print a distinct message ("Goroutine 1", "Goroutine 2", "Goroutine 3"). All messages should appear.
hints: Each goroutine needs its own `go` statement
The order of output is non-deterministic — goroutines run concurrently
Use enough sleep time for all goroutines to complete

verification.failureMessage: Make sure all three goroutines print their messages.

steps.title: Sync without wait group
steps.description: Use a channel to signal when a goroutine completes. The goroutine prints "Work done" then sends a value on a `chan bool`. Main receives before exiting.
hints: Have the goroutine send `done <- true` after printing
In main, use `<-done` to wait for the signal

verification.successMessage: You used a channel to synchronize your goroutine!
verification.failureMessage: Remember to send on the channel in the goroutine and receive in main.

steps.title: Goroutine with closure capture
steps.description: Launch a goroutine inside a loop that captures the loop variable correctly. Print "i = 0" through "i = 4" from goroutines.
hints: Loop variables in Go are reused — pass the value as an argument to avoid closure issues
Use `for i := 0; i < 5; i++ { go func(n int) { ... }(i) }`
Without copying the variable, all goroutines may see the final value

verification.successMessage: Correct! You avoided the closure capture pitfall.
verification.failureMessage: Make sure each goroutine receives its own copy of the loop variable.
